items.text: Mohammad Ghaedi, a lecturer in international relations, referring to the statements of Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, about Tehran's "unacceptable" demands, said that the Islamic Republic has not backed down from its previous demands even after the midterm elections, and the hope for a change in Tehran's position has not materialized. He added that Rubio considers the continuation of the naval blockade as a way to increase pressure, which might change the calculations of the Islamic Republic and the conditions for reaching an agreement.

Hossein Mohibi, spokesperson for the IRGC, said that no war mines have been cleared in the Strait of Hormuz and this claim is outright false. He added that no one dares to enter the Strait of Hormuz to clear mines. Mohibi also questioned how the US controls the Strait of Hormuz while several incidents happen daily to ships there.

The Indo-Pacific Defense Forum military magazine reported that China and Russia, despite claiming neutrality, support the Islamic Republic's war. According to the magazine, Russia has helped Tehran by providing satellite information and military and cyber cooperation, while China has assisted by supplying military equipment and purchasing Iranian oil. The report also mentioned trilateral cooperation between the Islamic Republic, China, and Russia in drone production.

Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, said Washington's actions in the region are "completely defensive" and if American forces or commercial ships are threatened, they will act to defend themselves. He considered the Islamic Republic's acquisition of nuclear weapons dangerous and unacceptable for the whole world and said Trump took responsibility for an action that previous presidents had failed to carry out.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said if Qatar's mediation realistically addresses the demands of both sides and focuses negotiations on the nuclear file, there is a possibility of progress in talks. He added that the Islamic Republic's demand to end all regional conflicts is not resolvable in talks with the US. Akbarin also said the Republican defeat in the midterm elections does not mean the end of Trump or the party, but the Islamic Republic believes it can prevent another attack by insisting on its positions.

The Human Rights Organization for Sports expressed concern in an open letter to the Asian Football Confederation about the death sentence issued for footballer Ehsan Hosseinipour Hesarlu, the imprisonment of Amir Reza Nasrazadani, and the arbitrary detention of several members of Iran's football community, calling for immediate action to protect their lives and safety. The organization highlighted violations of the right to a fair trial, denial of access to an independent lawyer, and restrictions on freedom of expression. It also emphasized the responsibility of the Asian Football Confederation and other sports bodies to support athletes facing the risk of arrest, imprisonment, and execution, urging immediate protection measures.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, said in a press conference on Tuesday, 18 Aban, that there is no difference between the parties for Iran because it has been hurt by both political factions in the US. He described Tehran's demands as logical and said the US must stop sanctions, naval blockade, and economic expulsion operations to start negotiations. Baqaei also stated that if the US meets the Islamic Republic's demands, security will return to the region within two days, and Iran's two-day plan remains on the table.

According to a report by Harana News Agency, some general crime prisoners in Tehran Grand Prison have been transferred to the political prisoners' section and involved in internal order management under the title "security." Assigning guarding and security duties to prisoners is prohibited by the executive regulations of the Prisons Organization. Informed sources have also reported violent confrontations and threats against some prisoners, including the beating of Seyed Mehdi Hosseini, a detainee from the December 1404 protests.

Los Angeles Lakers defeated Detroit Pistons 121-116 without their injured star Luka Doncic, securing their top position in the Western Conference. Austin Reaves led the team with 43 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists. Walker Kessler contributed 12 points, 16 rebounds, and 3 blocks in the final moments to ensure the Lakers' victory.
A video received by Iran International shows the poor condition of the dormitory at Gorgan University after the rain on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban.

The father of Paria Mehrmand, a 15-year-old basketball player injured in the overturning of the Sahar Academy team bus, reported the crushing of his daughter's leg and severe damage to its arteries and criticized the team's travel conditions, asking: "Who will be responsible to the families?" Also, the sister of another injured player said her sister was re-hospitalized due to severe pain after discharge. Families have demanded accountability from officials regarding this incident.
A video received by Iran International shows severe flooding in the streets of Gonbad Kavus city on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban.
A bookstore in Tehran was sealed due to "non-compliance with Islamic norms." This was reported by the HRANA news agency. An informed source confirmed this news.

According to reports, dental costs in Iran are high, with each tooth extraction costing 6 million Tomans and root canal treatment 12 to 15 million Tomans. The prices of some medications, such as "Migrakim" and "Amoxicillin," have also significantly increased. Health insurance has excluded some medications and services from coverage, and diabetic patients are facing difficulties in obtaining their medicines.
Videos received by Iran International show flooding entering public streets of Bushehr on Sunday, 17 Aban after rainfall.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that Donald Trump's statements about continuing economic pressure, negotiation, and the possibility of attacking Iran's infrastructure are pursued simultaneously and are not contradictory. He added that the Islamic Republic fears a renewed uprising of the people and hopes to get through the remaining two years of Trump's administration. He believes the regime is deluded about achieving a "win-win" agreement and that the current process is against national interests and leads to another war.

The head of the judiciary in Isfahan province announced the decision to block social media pages of bloggers and popular individuals. According to Jafari, those whose published content falls under categories such as actions against national security, public security, and public norms will face page blocking and legal prosecution. These statements indicate an expansion of judicial oversight over users and bloggers and a possible restriction of freedom of expression in cyberspace.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the recent US attacks on southern Iran can be seen as initial waves of an operation to weaken and destroy the Islamic Republic's air defenses. He added this operation could be to facilitate the passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz or prepare the field for broader air or even ground operations. Aghaei said the US used mostly inexpensive drones and Trump tries to end the war with less cost in favor of the US.
A video received by Iran International shows that the old Qazvin to Rasht road was flooded after rain on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban.

Hossein Kermanpour, director general of public relations at the Ministry of Health, said the health system is prepared to face potential consequences of an attack on nuclear facilities and emergency and treatment measures have been planned. He advised people not to look at the explosion light and to seek shelter in a safe place as soon as possible. He also warned that taking iodine tablets without official instructions may harm the thyroid gland.

On Monday, 18 Aban, a group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in the cities of Kermanshah and Isfahan. The protesting retirees demanded the full implementation of regulation 89/24, adjustment of salaries, and attention to their livelihood and medical issues.

Nima Dadgostar, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump, in an interview with the program "60 Minutes," accepted part of JD Vance's assessment about voters' dissatisfaction with the war and rising living costs, but emphasized that if he could go back, he would make the same decision regarding the attack on Iran. Trump also spoke about excessive strictness towards some undocumented immigrants and expressed readiness to negotiate with Democrats to find a solution.

Messages received by Iran International indicate continued drug price increases, shortages, and removal of some drugs from insurance coverage. A diabetic citizen said the price of his needed Iranian medicine has quadrupled in two months. Another citizen said he spends over five million tomans monthly on medicine, and the price of his seizure medication increased by 200,000 tomans in one week.
Videos sent to Iran International show that a group of retired employees of Bank Saderat gathered in Tehran on Sunday, 17 Aban to pursue their demands.

Donald Trump said his offer to Dana White to become White House spokesperson was not serious and was just a joke. Trump said Dana liked the idea and described her as amazing. White said she is already busy and did not comment on accepting the position.

Aban (Zeinab) Mousavi and her brother Hassan Mousavi, two citizens arrested in connection with the protests of Dey 1404, have been held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over eight months in judicial uncertainty. They face charges including "moharebeh" and no court has been held to address their charges so far. Temporary release on bail has also not been possible for them.

Hamidreza Goodarzi, representative of Aligudarz in the parliament, said that decisions about enriched uranium are made at the highest level of the country, and according to him, they will not deliver uranium under any circumstances. He added that if necessary, enrichment will be raised above 60 percent, and the Supreme National Security Council must decide on exiting the NPT to prevent the presence of IAEA inspectors. Goodarzi also said the enemy uses negotiations whenever it needs to breathe artificially.

Today, Monday, a group of workers from the National Iranian Steel Industrial Group gathered in the factory premises in Ahvaz. The protesters cited unpaid wage arrears, uncertainty in production status, and neglect of livelihood problems as reasons for holding this gathering.

Halvash news agency reported that a number of gas tanker drivers who have loaded their cargo for transfer to the Rimdan and Pishin borders of Pakistan remain uncertain at the Star of the Persian Gulf oil refinery in Bandar Abbas and have not been allowed to leave customs. A trade official also reported the stoppage of dozens of ships in northern ports and a threefold increase in maritime transport costs in the Caspian Sea.

Ziba Adeli, the technical director of the Sahar Academy women's basketball team, reported that 11 people were injured in the team's bus overturn accident and said that three players were injured in the spine area and the team may not be able to continue its presence in the Premier League. The team members were supposed to return from Khorramshahr to Tehran by train at 18:00 on Saturday, but due to a landslide and train cancellation, they traveled by bus which overturned near Shush. Paria Mehrmand and Somayeh Sabetzadeh suffered fractures and require surgery.

Today, continuing protests by retired telecommunications workers, some retirees gathered in the cities of Zanjan and Rasht and demanded attention to their demands. These gatherings were held in protest against ongoing livelihood problems and the unmet demands of retirees.

A video received by Iran International shows a funeral for a person titled "Unknown Martyr" held in the campus of Azad University of Karaj, and the attendees of this ceremony are shouting "Heydar, Heydar."

According to a report published by ILNA, some employed women face administrative and insurance problems in receiving their claims from the Social Security Organization and are forced to pursue legal action. A woman filed a complaint to increase the duration of maternity leave and receive full pay for this period from the Social Security Department of Khorasan Razavi province, and the judicial authorities ruled in her favor. Simin Yaghoubi, a women's labor rights activist, stated that delays in payment, incorrect calculations, and restrictive interpretations of laws lead to the violation of insured women's rights and weaken public trust in the social security system.

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the UAE president, said that reaching a comprehensive political agreement between the US and Iran seems difficult and the region should prepare for a long period of uncertainty. He added that the consequences of the war may last for a long time and the UAE must invest in defense capabilities and strengthening security partners. Gargash also said the UAE has opposed the US-Iran war from the start and thanked various countries for their support against Iranian attacks.

According to published videos, a group of retired telecommunications workers gathered on Tuesday, 18 Aban, in the cities of Isfahan, Zanjan, and Kermanshah to pursue their demands, shouting: "The Imam Command Headquarters, Etemadbamin Sepah, has taken our rights."

Hooman Shayani, a political detainee, has been held in Noorabad Mamasani prison for over 10 months without a trial. His judicial case remains unresolved and no court session has been held for him. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that in the US attack on Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan during the 12-day war, the adjacent buildings of Iran's nuclear facilities were destroyed but neither the centrifuge machines nor the 60% uranium were damaged. He added that both the Democratic and Republican parties aim to dominate Muslim and non-Muslim countries, with no difference in their goal, only in their methods. Kowsari said Democrats act gently while Republicans pursue their goals more openly.

Today, continuing the protests of telecommunications retirees, a group of these retirees held a protest gathering in the cities of Tehran, Hamedan, Sanandaj, and Bijar. The mentioned retirees stated addressing livelihood and medical problems among their demands.

Foreign ministers of the Group of Seven gathered for a two-day meeting in Paris. The possibility of escalating the crisis between the United States and the Islamic Republic is among the topics discussed at this meeting.

Mehdi Taj, head of the Iranian Football Federation, emphasized continued support for Amir Ghalenoei until the 2027 Asian Cup and mentioned possible changes in the national team's coaching staff, including adding a foreign assistant. He said that after the World Cup, both the senior national team and the U-23 team are undergoing reconstruction, with youth development alongside experience. Taj also confirmed that a foreign assistant will be added to the national team's coaching staff.

A video sent to Iran International shows that a group of families seeking justice for the January 2026 victims visited the graves of their loved ones on Monday, November 9, in the tenth month after the government's large massacre in that month.

Aref Khederlou, Director General of Renovation, Development, and Equipment of Schools in West Azerbaijan, stated that to reach the national average of 5.5 square meters of educational space per student, this province needs to build 972 new schools.

Police sealed a cafe in Baharestan for what they described as 'promoting corruption and prostitution' and arrested its operator. Several other businesses were also sealed, and sealing warnings were issued for seven units. The reasons given for these actions include failure to observe Islamic norms and regulations.

With the onset of cold weather and rainfall, schools in various parts of Iran are facing problems such as not turning on heating devices and students suffering from cold. It was reported that schools in Amol, Tehran, Abyek, and Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari do not turn on heating devices due to Ministry of Education directives, and some schools have not been closed. Students complain about the cold and lack of heating facilities and question why schools are not closed under these conditions.
The director of education in Khash county reported the identification of 590 children who have dropped out of school in this county.

Videos received by Iran International show that a group of car voucher holders gathered on Monday, 18 Aban, in protest against the non-issuance of invitation letters for pre-sold cars in Aban and the renewed price increase since registration, in front of the Iran Khodro sales organization in Tehran.

Information received by Iran International indicates that Mohammad Parsa Amini, a 17-year-old teenager who was killed in Dey 1404 while helping an injured protester, had previously been tortured during the "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests due to "turban throwing."
Iran International reports that Persepolis women's football team defeated Sepahan 1-0 in the seventh week of the Women's Premier League. The only goal of the match was scored by Somayeh Esmaeili.

Israel's Kan network reported that on Monday, 18 Aban, police began investigations after discovering threatening leaflets in mailboxes of residents in northern Tel Aviv, believed to originate from the Islamic Republic. The pro-Islamic Republic hacker group "Hanzala" claimed responsibility for distributing these leaflets. The leaflets contained a QR code directing recipients to the group's website, which warned Israel about attacks on Iran's energy infrastructure.

Gao Jiacon, spokesperson for China's Foreign Ministry, announced that Beijing is in contact with the US and Russia about a possible meeting of the presidents of China, the US, and Russia to discuss ending the war in Iran. He said that the prolongation of the conflict between Tehran and Washington benefits no one and that the parties should resolve their differences through dialogue.

An international conference titled "Women, Freedom, and Security" was held in the Federal Parliament of Germany in Berlin with the presence of human rights activists, political figures, and opponents of authoritarian governments. A report by Ali Hassanpour and an interview with Masih Alinejad from Iran International were presented.

Mehdi Farajpour, a Karagostar player, shared his joy with his mother after scoring the winning goal against Naft va Gaz Gachsaran. After the match, he went to his family and created an emotional moment by hugging his mother.

Ibrahim Kalin, head of Turkey's intelligence agency, said that Qatar will host a meeting next week between JD Vance, the US Vice President, and Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's National Security Council. Ankara considers this meeting a "key opportunity" for progress in negotiations. Kalin added that Turkey and regional mediators have proposed a 7-point plan for lifting sanctions and starting nuclear talks.

The Communications Office of Prince Reza Pahlavi announced that Matin Shabani, a young Iranian arrested during the December uprising, has been sentenced to death by the Islamic Republic court and faces imminent execution in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. The office described the court charges as fabricated and urged the public to raise their voices for this prisoner.

Fars News Agency, affiliated with the IRGC, reported citing an informed source that Ali Falih Al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, visited Tehran for a few hours on Friday, 15 Aban, and met with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament. According to the report, the Iraqi Prime Minister and his delegation discussed Baghdad's efforts to end the war with Iran with Ghalibaf. Fars quoted the source as saying that Ghalibaf emphasized the necessity of the US respecting Iran's rights within this plan to advance negotiations.

Soraya Talebi, the mother of Amirhossein Mousavi, a virtual activist sentenced to death, said her son was held in solitary confinement in Ward 209 of Evin Prison for 176 days after his arrest and was pressured for forced confession.

With the approach of the cold season, concerns about worsening gas shortages and increased power outages in Iran have grown. Officials of the Islamic Republic report limitations in energy supply and ask people to reduce their consumption. Mehdi Beigi, a member of the Iran International editorial team, examines the dimensions of the energy crisis in Iran and the government's plans to address it in "Peyvast".

Fuad Hussein, Iraq's foreign minister, said that Iraq's damages due to the Iran war and disruption in oil exports have reached 60 billion dollars. He added that the US Treasury Department has asked Baghdad to close all border crossings with Iran except two. Iraq has also reached an agreement with the US for the passage of its oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping route near Oman.
Ten months after the bloody Dey month of 1404, a group of families of the martyrs of the Iranian National Revolution gathered at the graves of their loved ones and commemorated them.
Today, the interrogation session of Amir Salar Davoodi, a lawyer, was held in Branch 11 of the Isfahan Prosecutor's Office.

Reuters reported on Monday, 18 Aban, citing a senior Iranian source, that the attacks on the evening of Sunday, 17 Aban, by the US on Qeshm Island targeted radar systems used in air defense and maritime navigation, missile launch bases, and naval mine systems. According to statistics from international maritime organizations released last week, attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz sharply increased in October and have continued at the highest rate since the start of the war.

The Criminal Court Two of Ardabil sentenced a defendant to three months and one day of imprisonment for the charge of "disobedience to government officers during duty." Due to the defendant's lack of prior criminal record, the sentence was converted to 540 hours of free public service at one of the elderly care centers in the city.

The official Iraqi news agency confirmed that the secret trip of Ali Faleh Al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, to Tehran on Friday, 15 Aban, was made to reduce tensions and prevent escalation of war in the region. Tasnim News Agency reported that after talks with Donald Trump and Tom Barrack, Ali Al-Zaydi met with Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran. It was also reported that Faleh Fayadh and Hadi Al-Amiri accompanied the Prime Minister on this trip.

Kosar Eftekhari, an eye injury victim of the nationwide protests, said at the international meeting "Women, Freedom, and Security" that the cries of those who are living evidence of the Islamic Republic's crimes must be heard. She added that they were shot in the eyes to silence them, but they will not allow this to happen and will continue the struggle.

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the UAE president, said at the Abu Dhabi Strategic Dialogue on November 9 that the Middle East may face a prolonged period of instability because reaching a comprehensive political agreement between the US and Iran to end a war lasting over eight months seems difficult. Gargash added that the UAE has opposed the US war against Iran from the beginning.
Amanollah Baloochi and Hafez Abdulrahim Koohi, two Sunni clerics, were sent on leave from Zahedan prison.

Teddy Riner, a five-time Olympic gold medalist, officially announced his entry into the 2027 French presidential election campaign in a video posted on the social network X. He has founded a new party called "The France We Want" and considers himself a worthy candidate. Riner criticized the current state of his country and expressed concern about the spread of fear, France's debt burden, and the decline of government authority.

An explosion at the HABAŞ steel factory in the Aliağa district of İzmir province, Turkey, around noon on Monday, 18 Aban, led to a large fire and a massive column of smoke. Initial reports suggest that an overhead crane may have broken and fallen into the furnace while pouring molten steel, causing the explosion. Three people were killed and 14 injured, with 10 trapped under debris, and rescue teams are trying to reach them.

The Canadian government approved a new package of economic sanctions against 38 entities and 24 individuals linked to ballistic missile industries, cyber activities, and financial networks supporting Russia's war in Ukraine. Mahsa Mortazavi, a reporter for Iran International, reports.

According to IRNA, Sarfirouzabad district in Kermanshah, with 249 villages and a population of about 32,000, faces extensive shortages in water, roads, electricity, telecommunications, education, and healthcare services. IRNA reported that about 60 villages experience water stress, and water for 47 villages is supplied by tankers. Additionally, a lack of schools and educational facilities has forced some students to travel long distances to continue their education.

A video shows the mother of Sajedeh Karimi mourning while holding her daughter's bullet-ridden clothes ten months after her death. Sajedeh Karimi, 17 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 near Astaneh Ashrafiyeh.

Dariush Barani Biranvand, mayor of Khorramabad, announced that about 500 to 600 worn-out taxis are active in this city and that renewing the public transportation fleet requires financial and credit resources.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, on Monday, 18 Aban, identified the IRGC as responsible for the recent cyberattack on refrigerators in chain stores in France and warned that this action would have consequences for Iran. Barrot accused the IRGC of involvement in the attack but did not provide further details about possible consequences. Meanwhile, the Paris prosecutor's office requested international arrest warrants for the commander of the offensive cyber unit "Shaheed Kaveh" affiliated with the IRGC and two of his deputies.

UN experts expressed concern about increasing judicial and security pressures on independent lawyers, restricting their access to clients and cases, and interfering with the independence of bar associations. They also criticized pressure on female lawyers due to mandatory hijab requirements and preventing independent lawyers from participating in some political cases. According to a report by Harana, at least 135 lawyers faced judicial and security actions between Shahrivar 1404 and Shahrivar 1405.

Esteghlal Club announced that Alireza Koushki, a player of Esteghlal football team, after surgery due to respiratory problems in Ahvaz, traveled by land to Gachsaran to spend some time with his family. This player will go to Tehran for further treatment and medical care. Esteghlal Club wished him a full recovery.

Shirin Ebadi, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, announced that she dedicated her 29th honorary doctorate, received from Domingo Faustino Sarmiento University in Buenos Aires, Argentina, to the mothers seeking justice who lost their children in Dey 1404. Ebadi wrote in a message that she dedicates this honor to the mothers seeking justice who lost their children in Dey 1404. She also called for the establishment of democracy in Iran during her speech at the university and stated that the Iranian people oppose the government's policies that expose the country to tension and war.

Tehran Prosecutor's Office announced a judicial case against a gynecologist due to a video about the birth of four babies from single mothers. The doctor faces the charge of "spreading falsehoods" and their social media page has been blocked.

Fatemeh Sepahri, a political prisoner in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, continues to be deprived of specialized medical care and transfer to medical centers outside the prison despite multiple physical problems. Her brother stated that Fatemeh Sepahri reported severe pain in her right hand and the prison doctor prescribed an MRI, but no action has been taken to perform it so far.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Islamic Republic's Parliament, wrote on the social network X on Monday, 18 Aban, that Israelis are trying day and night to involve the United States in an endless war with the Islamic Republic. Ghalibaf wrote: "A quagmire that no president, whether now or in the future, whether Republican or Democrat, can get out of."

In two work-related incidents in the cities of Bonab and Mashhad, two workers died. One of them died in a beam and block production factory in Bonab while working with a concrete press machine, and the other died due to a wall collapse during demolition operations in Mashhad.

Behnam Taleblu, senior director of the Iran program at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said that Donald Trump, by keeping diplomacy open and maintaining the military option, is seeking the least costly way to confront the Islamic Republic. According to him, the mediation efforts of Qatar and other Arab countries may delay a US military attack for several weeks or months, but cannot alone prevent a conflict. Taleblu added that the Trump administration, simultaneously with negotiations, continues the policy of maximum pressure and economic siege of the Islamic Republic, and that diplomacy alone is not sufficient to achieve America's strategic goals.

Farzin Dabiri, a member of the Football Federation's board, was suspended from the board membership and football activities until further notice due to not standing during the national anthem at Hamid Alidousti's funeral ceremony. The judicial authorities of the Football Federation held a meeting on Monday and suspended Dabiri's membership until the next board meeting on 9 Dey. Additionally, all of Farzin Dabiri's football activities were banned until further notice.

The execution of a 21-year-old prisoner was carried out in Behshahr prison. The tenth branch of the Criminal Court One of Tehran province sentenced a defendant in the case of killing a police officer to death. Additionally, three prisoners sentenced to death in separate cases were released from execution with the consent of the victims' families.

On Monday, 18 Aban, retired telecommunications workers held protests in 10 cities demanding full implementation of regulation 89/24 and salary adjustments. Also, workers of the National Industrial Steel Group of Iran in Ahvaz protested unpaid overdue wages and marched after gathering at the factory.
An audio version of Titrawal with Niusha Sarami was released about the meeting between Trump and the Prime Minister of Qatar and the involvement of China, Russia, and Turkey to prevent war.

Reza Tayebnia, a lawyer, was sentenced to six months in prison by Branch 103 of the Criminal Court Two of Kohgiluyeh County. The sentence was issued on the charge of "propaganda against the regime." This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said the US "Iron Gates" plan is designed to prevent the transfer of advanced weapons and dual-use technologies through land borders and the Caspian Sea. He added the plan could disrupt financing of proxy groups and reconstruction of the Islamic Republic's arms industries and seems to target military equipment transfers from Russia and China with neighboring countries' cooperation. Mahdavi-Azad emphasized the plan may go beyond sanctions and be a significant military step in US pressure on the Islamic Republic.

Majid Aflaki, head coach of Iran's national taekwondo team at the Paris 2024 Olympics, said that because he posted a protest story in Dey month, he was told not to come to the national team's training anymore. The Iranian national team, under his leadership, won one gold, two silver, and one bronze at the Paris Olympics. Aflaki also led the national team to Asian and World Cup championships and earned the title of best coach in Asia.
Iran International reported that an audio version of Cheshmandaz titled "Iron Gates" has been released, addressing the new US plan to suffocate the IRGC.

Najmeh Amini, a 23-year-old student sentenced to death, remains in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. An appeal has been filed against her death sentence, and the Supreme Court has not yet made a decision regarding it. She has also been sentenced to imprisonment in a separate case.

A video shows a citizen releasing two white balloons in memory of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi, executed protesters. These two protesters were among 12 defendants in the "Alikhani Square" case in Isfahan who were sentenced to death.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the large gap between Tehran's and Washington's demands has made reaching a diplomatic agreement difficult. He added that the Islamic Republic is neither certain of the war being averted nor hopeful for the success of negotiations. Rahimpour also said that the results of the US midterm elections and political developments in Israel may affect the timing and manner of military actions but do not mean weakening Washington's and Tel Aviv's positions.

Adel Ferdosipour reacted to criticism about not standing during the national anthem at Hamid Alidousti's funeral on Football 360, saying the accusations do not stick to him and he has always loved his country. He added that despite facing restrictions, he has tried to stay in Iran and attract talented youth. He called the criticisms unfair and emphasized that Iran is his red line.

Donald Trump, after talks with the Prime Minister of Qatar, said that Qatar prefers the Iran issue to be resolved peacefully, but the US is ready for military strikes if necessary. Trump added that Saudi Arabia also prefers a peaceful resolution to the conflict with the Islamic Republic. He also defended Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, saying Hegseth has won two wars.

Alhurra network, quoting a source in the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, reported that the Islamic Republic has introduced Abdolreza Mesgariyan, commander of the Ramadan Base of the Quds Force, as its new ambassador in Baghdad. He is to replace Mohammad Kazem Al-Sadegh, but the start date of his mission is not yet clear. Mesgariyan is responsible for security coordination between Tehran, Baghdad, and Erbil and also coordinates with Iraqi armed groups close to Tehran.

Iran International reported that Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, said on Football Bartar that Ramin Rezaeian's departure from the team was for financial reasons, but he did not agree with the departure and the club supported him.

Trump said he had a very good conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Prime Minister of Qatar, during which many issues related to the Islamic Republic of Iran were discussed. He stated that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and other countries prefer to maintain the current situation, meaning the largest naval blockade in history and the new "Iron Gate" operation will continue. Trump emphasized that everyone agreed Iran cannot have nuclear weapons and the United States is fully armed and ready to act if there are any changes in the Middle East.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the Chinese are trying to hold a trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping, and Putin in China, with one of the main topics being Iran and the future of the Islamic Republic. He asked whether China will become a second Guadeloupe and whether the fate of the Islamic Republic will be decided at the table of the three major world powers, and whether China and Russia are willing to sacrifice the Islamic Republic in a bigger deal with the US.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the President of the UAE, warned that there is no solution available for regional conflicts and the Middle East is likely heading towards a period of instability and unrest; the UAE is preparing itself for the worst-case scenario.

Trump said on Truth Social that he had a "very good" contact with the Prime Minister of Qatar about the Islamic Republic. He added that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait, and other countries prefer to maintain the "status quo" regarding Iran. Trump also said that the largest naval blockade in history will continue and a new Iron Gate operation will be carried out, with operations continuing both on land and at sea.

Trump said in a White House press conference that the Islamic Republic, in addition to killing many American citizens, has killed "at least 75,000 protesters." He added that if they have to act again, they are in full military readiness and prepared to take action. Trump also said the conflict with the Islamic Republic is "quickly coming to an end" and that Iran will never obtain nuclear weapons.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that competition for power within the Islamic Republic has intensified. He added that Mohsen Rezaei's influence is increasing while Qalibaf's power is decreasing. He also said that Mohsen Rezaei is trying to take control of the equations with the US, Russia, and China.

Jean-Noël Barrot, the French Foreign Minister, identified the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as responsible for cyberattacks on the cooling systems of hundreds of food stores in France and warned that the Islamic Republic would face consequences for this action. Simultaneously, the Paris prosecutor's office has launched an investigation into the possible role of the hacking group known as "Shahid Kaveh" in these attacks.

Mohsen Rezaee wrote on X that the Iran war has shattered the US government and told Washington that the time has come to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly presented. He urged Washington to stop its desperate gambling and cease producing fake news about imaginary negotiations.

France says the IRGC hacked supermarket refrigerators in the country. The French foreign minister summoned the ambassador of the Islamic Republic and said this attack will have consequences for Tehran.

Iraq's state news agency reported that the country will temporarily close the Mandali border crossing with Iran from Friday to complete technical requirements. The report did not provide further details. In recent weeks, several border crossings between Iran and Iraq have been temporarily closed.

Trump said Iran's production capability has been severely reduced, with about 85% of this capability lost. He suggested that the conflict with Iran may soon end and emphasized that the US is fully armed and ready to act. Trump also stated that Iran will never have nuclear weapons and that the US has established the largest military blockade in history.

Donald Trump, after meeting with the Prime Minister of Qatar, announced that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait, and other regional countries want to continue the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the Iron Gate operation. Trump added that these countries agree on preventing the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons and reported progress toward ending the war. He said the US remains ready for military action but currently considers it unlikely.

Trump defended US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth against impeachment efforts, praising his military operations against Iran and Venezuela. Trump wrote on Truth Social that army recruitment has reached its highest level in history and that there have been two victories in Venezuela and Iran. He also called Republican Congressman Thomas Massey, who is pushing for Hegseth's impeachment, a "total loser."

Prince Reza Pahlavi described the Islamic Republic as a combination of the totalitarian features of the Soviet Union, Hitler's fascism, and the racist apartheid system during a press conference in Krakow, Poland. He emphasized that the international community has so far not taken decisive action against the Islamic Republic.

Trump said in an interview with C-SPAN that the reason for his current approach toward Iran is dialogue with regional countries and their preference to continue this approach instead of another attack. He said this attack would be "almost five times larger than the first attack." Trump added that in talks with these countries, he found they prefer the issue to proceed in this way and said, "Therefore, I also prefer to proceed in this way."

Erfan Ghanei-Fard, a Middle East analyst, said Tehran is changing its influence model in Iraq from political management of proxy forces to operational and security focus. He added this appointment aims to rebuild the command of proxy networks, control Iraqi armed groups, and keep Iraq as the Islamic Republic's backyard against the US and Israel.

Economic consequences of the war have intensified the unemployment crisis in Iran, pushing some dismissed workers to daily wage labor and street work. According to initial estimates by the Ministry of Labor of the Islamic Republic, over one million jobs have been lost during the war and about two million people have become unemployed directly and indirectly. Rouzbeh Boulehri explains the possibility of this number of unemployed people using unemployment insurance.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, said Donald Trump has the opportunity to expand military operations against the Islamic Republic before the new Congress begins its work, without potential congressional restrictions. He also said Baghdad does not have full control over armed groups affiliated with the Islamic Republic, and the best scenario for Iraq is the removal of the Islamic Republic and the possibility of exercising national sovereignty over these groups.

UN human rights experts, referring to security and judicial actions against at least 135 lawyers in Iran over the past year, called for the immediate cessation of arrests and intimidation of independent lawyers.

Gholamreza Mesbahi-Moghadam, a member of the Expediency Discernment Council, said that the patience and endurance of the people against economic difficulties imposed by the enemy to exhaust citizens have led the people to choose the path of resistance. He added that the Iranian nation, aware of the enemy's plan, has chosen resistance. Mesbahi-Moghadam also said that despite the ethnic and religious diversity in Iran, people agree on the axis of Islam and Iran, and the leadership has emphasized that criticisms should be expressed as concern, not as protests.

The Wall Street Journal reported from informed sources that following a threat from the Islamic Republic, the United States removed its military aircraft from a British airbase for the second time. American officials are still examining the exact nature of the threat against the RAF Mildenhall airbase in Britain. It is not yet clear whether the threat was immediate or more general in nature.

China's Foreign Ministry announced that Beijing is in contact with relevant parties about the possibility of holding a summit of the leaders of the US, Russia, and China aimed at ending the war with the Islamic Republic. China emphasized that the continuation of the war benefits neither side nor the international community and stressed the necessity of ending the conflicts.

Rouhollah Motafakker Azad, a member of the Parliament's presidium, said if the enemy makes a new mistake, the war will have bigger surprises for them. He added that all options to defend the country remain on the table. Motafakker Azad also said the armed forces have become more successful and precise in each war.
